tagline: Big-island Greece: Minoan ruins, gorge hikes, pink-sand lagoons and long tavern nights.

items.title: Palace of Knossos
items.desc: The 4,000-year-old Minoan palace outside Heraklion - go at opening before the heat and the crowds.

items.title: Chania old harbour
items.desc: Venetian lighthouse, pastel waterfront and alley mazes - prettiest at golden hour.

items.title: Balos Lagoon
items.desc: Turquoise-and-white lagoon on the northwest tip; boat from Kissamos or a bumpy drive plus hike.

items.title: Samaria Gorge hike
items.desc: 16 km through Europe's longest gorge, ending at the Libyan Sea - ferry back from Agia Roumeli.

items.title: Elafonisi beach day
items.desc: Pink sand and a wade-across lagoon in the far southwest; rent a car and make a day of it.

items.title: Preveli palm beach
items.desc: A river with palm forest meets the sea below a clifftop monastery - swim upstream.

items.title: Cretan taverna crawl
items.desc: Order dakos, slow-cooked lamb and raki; village tavernas around Vamos beat the tourist strips.

items.title: Heraklion central market
items.desc: Odos 1866 market street for olive oil, mountain honey, graviera cheese and herb bundles.

items.title: Chania old-town bars
items.desc: Start with cocktails on the harbour wall, then move into the leather-district lanes after midnight.

items.title: Malia strip
items.desc: Crete's full-throttle club strip - big rooms, foam nights and sunrise gyros. Pace yourself.

items.title: Rakadiko evening
items.desc: A meze-and-raki house where plates keep arriving as long as you keep drinking - live lyra if you're lucky.

tagline: Caldera-edge villages, volcanic beaches and the most photographed sunset in Greece.

items.title: Oia sunset
items.desc: Claim a caldera-edge spot an hour early, or dodge the crowds by watching from a catamaran instead.

items.title: Akrotiri ruins
items.desc: A Bronze-Age town preserved in volcanic ash - Greece's Pompeii, under a cool roofed dig.

items.title: Fira to Oia caldera hike
items.desc: 10 km along the crater rim through Imerovigli; three hours of the best views on the island.

items.title: Catamaran + hot springs
items.desc: Sail the caldera, swim at the volcanic hot springs and eat grilled fish off the back of the boat.

items.title: Red Beach & Perissa
items.desc: Crimson cliffs at Akrotiri, then black-sand lounging and beach bars on the east coast.

items.title: Assyrtiko wine tasting
items.desc: Volcanic-soil whites at Santo Wines or Venetsanos, both perched on the caldera edge.

items.title: Tomatokeftedes & fava
items.desc: Santorini's own tomato fritters and yellow split-pea puree - best in Megalochori's tavernas.

items.title: Fira bar quarter
items.desc: Caldera-view cocktail terraces early, then tiny loud bars stacked down the cliff lanes late.

items.title: Open-air cinema Kamari
items.desc: A movie under vines with wine in hand - the mellow alternative to a club night.

tagline: Ancient rock, anarchic street art and rooftops that all point at the Parthenon.

items.title: Acropolis at opening
items.desc: Be at the gate for 8am - you get the Parthenon in soft light and beat the cruise crowds.

items.title: Acropolis Museum
items.desc: Glass floors over the dig site and the Parthenon frieze at eye level.

items.title: Plaka & Anafiotika wander
items.desc: Island-style whitewashed lanes hiding under the Acropolis rock - get lost on purpose.

items.title: Lycabettus Hill climb
items.desc: Hike or funicular up for a 360 view; the Acropolis floats over the city at dusk.

items.title: Varvakios market lunch
items.desc: The central meat-and-fish market, ringed by no-menu tavernas ladling out magiritsa and stews.

items.title: Souvlaki in Monastiraki
items.desc: The eternal debate - Kostas vs Bairaktaris. Eat both, decide yourself.

items.title: Koukaki & Psyrri bars
items.desc: Third-wave cocktail bars, ouzeries and live rebetiko packed into a few walkable blocks.

items.title: Rooftop cinema Thision
items.desc: Open-air films with the lit Parthenon behind the screen, May to October.

tagline: The classics earn the hype - then the neighbourhoods take over.

items.title: Louvre (one wing only)
items.desc: Pick a single wing and two hours - trying to 'do' the Louvre ruins it. Book a timed slot.

items.title: Eiffel Tower at sparkle
items.desc: Skip the queue: watch the on-the-hour night sparkle from Trocadero or a Seine bank picnic.

items.title: Sainte-Chapelle
items.desc: A jewel box of 13th-century stained glass most visitors walk straight past.

items.title: Montmartre morning
items.desc: Climb to Sacre-Coeur before 9am, then coffee on Place du Tertre as the easels come out.

items.title: Seine-side cycle
items.desc: Rent a Velib and ride the car-free river expressway from Notre-Dame to the Eiffel Tower.

items.title: Marche des Enfants Rouges
items.desc: Paris's oldest covered market - Moroccan, Japanese and Lebanese stalls in the Marais.

items.title: Classic bistro dinner
items.desc: Steak frites, natural wine and zero rush - book Chez Janou or Bistrot Paul Bert ahead.

items.title: Oberkampf bar run
items.desc: Rue Oberkampf and Rue Jean-Pierre Timbaud chain dive bars, cocktail dens and late DJs.

items.title: Jazz on Rue des Lombards
items.desc: Three legendary clubs on one street - Duc des Lombards for the classy set, sunset sessions till late.

tagline: A 2,700-year open-air museum where dinner is the second religion.

items.title: Colosseum underground
items.desc: Book the arena-floor-and-hypogeum ticket - the standard entry misses the best part.

items.title: Pantheon
items.desc: Two thousand years old, still the world's largest unreinforced dome. Go when it rains.

items.title: Vatican at dawn
items.desc: First-entry Sistine Chapel slot, then St Peter's dome climb before the square fills.

items.title: Trastevere wander
items.desc: Ochre lanes, laundry lines and piazza life - cross the river and put the map away.

items.title: Appian Way by bike
items.desc: Cycle the ancient road past catacombs and aqueduct ruins - Sundays it's car-free.

items.title: Cacio e pepe pilgrimage
items.desc: Roman pasta's holy trinity - carbonara, amatriciana, cacio e pepe - done right in Testaccio.

items.title: Gelato standards
items.desc: Look for lids on the tubs and muted colours - Otaleg and Gelateria dei Gracchi, not the neon piles.

items.title: Aperitivo in Monti
items.desc: Spritz and free snacks from 6pm on Piazza della Madonna dei Monti, then wine bars till late.

items.title: Testaccio clubs
items.desc: Rome's nightlife hill - stacked clubs inside an old slaughterhouse district, going till 4am.

tagline: Gaudi fever dreams, beach afternoons and dinners that start at 10pm.

items.title: Sagrada Familia
items.desc: Book the earliest slot with tower access - the light through the stained glass is the whole point.

items.title: Park Guell
items.desc: Gaudi's mosaic hilltop park - timed entry required, sunset slots go first.

items.title: Gothic Quarter
items.desc: Roman walls to medieval squares in ten minutes of alleys - Placa Sant Felip Neri is the quiet gem.

items.title: Bunkers del Carmel sunset
items.desc: Old anti-aircraft bunkers with the city grid rolling to the sea - bring drinks, everyone does.

items.title: Barceloneta beach morning
items.desc: Swim early, then chiringuito vermouth at noon before the crowds swallow the sand.

items.title: La Boqueria (early)
items.desc: The Rambla market at 8am is a food cathedral; by 11 it's a selfie corridor.

items.title: Tapas crawl in El Born
items.desc: Standing-room bars: pintxos at Euskal Etxea, bombas at La Cova Fumada, cava everywhere.

items.title: Gracia plaza-hopping
items.desc: Neighbourhood squares full of terrace tables until 2am - Placa del Sol is ground zero.

items.title: Razzmatazz
items.desc: Five clubs in one warehouse - indie, techno and whatever the fifth room is doing that night.

tagline: Seven hills, tiled facades, custard tarts and the Atlantic light everyone talks about.

items.title: Alfama & the miradouros
items.desc: Lisbon's oldest quarter - climb from the cathedral to Miradouro da Graca for the postcard view.

items.title: Belem in a morning
items.desc: Jeronimos Monastery, the Discoveries monument and the original Pasteis de Belem, still warm.

items.title: Tram 28 (or walk it)
items.desc: The classic rattling route through Alfama and Estrela - or walk the line to skip pickpocket bingo.

items.title: Day trip to Sintra
items.desc: Pena Palace's candy-coloured towers in the forest mist - first train out, palace at opening.

items.title: LX Factory browse
items.desc: Industrial complex turned bookshops, murals and brunch under the 25 de Abril bridge.

items.title: Time Out Market
items.desc: The city's best chefs in one hall - go weekday lunch, weekends are scrums.

items.title: Ginjinha standing shot
items.desc: Sour-cherry liqueur from a hole-in-the-wall counter by Rossio - one euro, drunk on the pavement.

items.title: Bairro Alto crawl
items.desc: Hundreds of matchbox bars, drinks in hand in the street - it doesn't start before midnight.

items.title: Fado in a tasca
items.desc: Candle-lit mournful singing over wine in Alfama - Tasca do Chico is the raw, unticketed way in.

tagline: Canals, bikes, world-class art and brown cafes that haven't changed in a century.

items.title: Rijksmuseum
items.desc: Rembrandt's Night Watch and two floors of Golden Age swagger - book the first slot.

items.title: Anne Frank House
items.desc: Tickets release six weeks ahead and vanish in minutes - set an alarm, it's worth it.

items.title: Jordaan canals
items.desc: The prettiest ring of gables and houseboats - Prinsengracht at dusk is the shot.

items.title: Bike like a local
items.desc: Rent for the whole stay and ride to Amsterdam-Noord on the free ferry behind Centraal.

items.title: Vondelpark morning
items.desc: Coffee, herons and half the city jogging past - the calm before museum queues.

items.title: Albert Cuyp market
items.desc: Stroopwafels made in front of you, herring if you're brave, and De Pijp's cafes all around.

items.title: Indonesian rijsttafel
items.desc: The colonial-era 'rice table' of twenty small dishes - Amsterdam does it better than anywhere in Europe.

items.title: Brown cafe evening
items.desc: Centuries-old wood-panelled pubs - candlelight, local beer and bar cats at Cafe Hoppe or 't Smalle.

items.title: Paradiso gig
items.desc: A converted church that's hosted everyone from Bowie to techno all-nighters - check the listings.

tagline: A fairytale skyline, the world's best beer culture, and it's all walkable.

items.title: Charles Bridge at dawn
items.desc: 6am gets you the statues, the mist and no crowds - by 10 it's a procession.

items.title: Prague Castle complex
items.desc: St Vitus Cathedral's stained glass and the Golden Lane - go up via the vineyard steps.

items.title: Old Town Square & clock
items.desc: The Astronomical Clock's hourly show is famously underwhelming - the square itself is not.

items.title: Petrin Hill & tower
items.desc: Funicular up through orchards to a mini Eiffel Tower with the whole red-roofed city below.

items.title: Vltava paddle boat
items.desc: Rent a swan pedalo at sunset - the castle lit up from the water is absurdly good.

items.title: Lokal beer hall
items.desc: Tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell and svickova dumplings - the benchmark Czech pub meal.

items.title: Manifesto food market
items.desc: Shipping-container street food and natural wine when you need a schnitzel break.

items.title: Zizkov pub crawl
items.desc: The district with more pubs per head than anywhere on earth - dive in anywhere and drift.

items.title: Cross Club
items.desc: A steampunk sculpture you can dance inside - drum & bass in the industrial north.

tagline: Free world-class museums, market food from everywhere, and a pub for every mood.

items.title: British Museum highlights
items.desc: Rosetta Stone, Parthenon marbles, Sutton Hoo - free entry, go at 10am on a weekday.

items.title: Tower of London + bridge
items.desc: Crown Jewels first at opening, then walk Tower Bridge's glass walkway.

items.title: Westminster sweep
items.desc: Big Ben, the Abbey and a river walk to the South Bank - the postcard mile in two hours.

items.title: Borough Market graze
items.desc: London's great food market - toastie at Kappacasein, doughnuts at Bread Ahead, eyes bigger than stomach.

items.title: Regent's Canal walk
items.desc: Little Venice to Camden by towpath - narrowboats, Regent's Park's back door and market chaos at the end.

items.title: Brick Lane & Spitalfields
items.desc: Beigels at 3am, curry row, vintage stalls and street art in one East End wander.

items.title: Proper Sunday roast
items.desc: Yorkshire puddings the size of hats - book a gastropub like The Camberwell Arms by Thursday.

items.title: Soho into the small hours
items.desc: Theatre, then cocktail basements and jazz at Ronnie Scott's - the West End doesn't really close.

items.title: Fabric or Printworks-scale club
items.desc: London's superclubs still set the standard - book ahead, bring ID, expect a queue.

tagline: Base camp for waterfalls, black beaches and the northern lights - with a surprising bar scene.

items.title: Golden Circle
items.desc: Thingvellir rift valley, Geysir and Gullfoss in one loop - self-drive beats the bus.

items.title: South coast day
items.desc: Seljalandsfoss (walk behind it), Skogafoss, and Reynisfjara's black sand and basalt columns.

items.title: Hallgrimskirkja tower
items.desc: The rocket-shaped church - ride the lift for Reykjavik's rainbow rooftops.

items.title: Northern lights hunt
items.desc: September to March: check the aurora forecast, drive out of the light dome, be patient.

items.title: Sky Lagoon or Blue Lagoon
items.desc: Geothermal soaking with a swim-up bar - Sky Lagoon's cliff-edge infinity pool is the local pick.

items.title: Whale watching from the harbour
items.desc: Humpbacks and minkes in Faxafloi bay, April to October - dress like it's winter anyway.

items.title: Hot dog at Baejarins Beztu
items.desc: The famous harbour stand - order 'one with everything' like everyone since 1937.

items.title: Icelandic tasting menu
items.desc: Lamb, langoustine and skyr done seriously - Dill or Matur og Drykkur if the budget stretches.

items.title: Laugavegur runtur
items.desc: Reykjavik's weekend bar crawl - locals hit the same five bars in rotation until 4:30am.

items.title: Live music at Kex
items.desc: A hostel bar in an old biscuit factory with harbour views and free gigs most nights.

tagline: The world's biggest city, somehow the most orderly - and the best food city on earth.

items.title: Senso-ji at dawn
items.desc: Asakusa's great temple before the shops open - incense, lanterns and almost no one there.

items.title: Shibuya Crossing + Sky
items.desc: Do the scramble at street level, then watch it from Shibuya Sky's open roof at sunset.

items.title: Meiji Shrine & Harajuku
items.desc: A forest shrine and Tokyo's loudest fashion street, separated by one footbridge.

items.title: TeamLab Planets
items.desc: Barefoot, waist-deep in mirrored water-light rooms - book weeks ahead.

items.title: Day trip: Kamakura or Nikko
items.desc: Giant Buddha and surf beaches, or mountain shrines in cedar forest - both an easy train ride.

items.title: Tsukiji outer market breakfast
items.desc: Tamago skewers, uni bowls and knife shops - go hungry at 8am.

items.title: Ramen pilgrimage
items.desc: Ticket-machine counters everywhere - one tonkotsu, one shoyu, one tsukemen minimum.

items.title: Depachika basement
items.desc: Department-store food halls of terrifying perfection - assemble a picnic for Yoyogi Park.

items.title: Golden Gai
items.desc: Two hundred bars the size of closets in six Shinjuku alleys - find one with five seats and stay.

items.title: Karaoke till the last train (or first)
items.desc: Private-room karaoke with a drinks phone - the true Tokyo night ends at 5am with the first Yamanote train.

tagline: Ten thousand shrines, bamboo groves and geisha lanes - Japan's old soul.

items.title: Fushimi Inari at sunrise
items.desc: The ten thousand vermilion gates - start before 7am and hike past the crowds to the summit.

items.title: Kinkaku-ji
items.desc: The Golden Pavilion floating on its mirror pond - short visit, unforgettable.

items.title: Arashiyama bamboo grove
items.desc: Go at dawn, then escape uphill to the monkey park and the Hozu river gorge.

items.title: Philosopher's Path
items.desc: A canal-side walk linking temples from Ginkaku-ji south - cherry blossom central in April.

items.title: Tea ceremony in a machiya
items.desc: A proper whisked-matcha ceremony in a wooden townhouse - book a small-group session.

items.title: Nishiki Market
items.desc: Four hundred metres of pickles, yuba, tako-tamago and knives - Kyoto's kitchen since 1310.

items.title: Kaiseki splurge
items.desc: The multi-course seasonal art form was invented here - lunch kaiseki is half the dinner price.

items.title: Gion at dusk
items.desc: Lantern-lit Hanamikoji street as geiko hurry to appointments - respectful distance, no flash.

items.title: Pontocho alley dinner
items.desc: A single lantern-lit lane of riverside terraces - pick anywhere with kawadoko deck seating in summer.

tagline: Gold temples, canal mazes and the best street food per square metre anywhere.

items.title: Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew
items.desc: The Emerald Buddha and acres of gold - cover shoulders and knees, go at 8:30 opening.

items.title: Wat Arun at sunset
items.desc: Cross the river by 4-baht ferry and watch the porcelain spire catch fire from the far bank.

items.title: Wat Pho reclining Buddha
items.desc: 46 metres of gold leaf, then a traditional massage at the temple's own school.

items.title: Klong canal longtail ride
items.desc: Hire a longtail through Thonburi's canals - stilt houses and monitor lizards, old Bangkok.

items.title: Chatuchak weekend market
items.desc: 15,000 stalls of everything - go early, follow the coconut ice cream.

items.title: Chinatown street feast
items.desc: Yaowarat Road after dark: crab omelettes, satay smoke and Michelin-listed hawkers.

items.title: Boat noodles at Victory Monument
items.desc: Tiny intense bowls, eaten by the stack - four bowls is a start, ten is respect.

items.title: Rooftop sky bar
items.desc: Cocktails 60 floors up - Vertigo or Octave. Dress code: no shorts or flip-flops.

items.title: Khao San vs Thonglor
items.desc: Backpacker chaos on Khao San, or craft cocktails and clubs where Bangkok actually parties in Thonglor.

tagline: Jungle temples, rice-terrace mornings, surf sunsets and cliff-edge dance fires.

items.title: Tegalalang rice terraces
items.desc: The layered emerald bowls north of Ubud - 7am light, before the swing crowds arrive.

items.title: Uluwatu temple & kecak
items.desc: Clifftop temple, thieving monkeys, and the sunset fire-chant kecak dance - book the 6pm show.

items.title: Tirta Empul water temple
items.desc: Join the purification ritual in the spring-fed pools - sarongs provided, respect required.

items.title: Mount Batur sunrise trek
items.desc: 2am pickup, headlamp climb, sunrise above a crater lake with eggs steamed in volcano vents.

items.title: Learn to surf in Canggu
items.desc: Mellow beach breaks and cheap board hire - Batu Bolong is the classic learner wave.

items.title: Ubud jungle spa day
items.desc: Flower baths and massage pavilions over the Campuhan river valley - book a half day.

items.title: Babi guling lunch
items.desc: Balinese roast suckling pig - Warung Ibu Oka in Ubud is the famous one, village warungs the real one.

items.title: Warung nasi campur
items.desc: Point at what looks good, pay three dollars, repeat daily.

items.title: Canggu beach bars
items.desc: Sunset beers on beanbags at Batu Bolong, then Old Man's or The Lawn until the DJs stop.

items.title: Jungle party in Ubud
items.desc: Full-moon and jungle-club nights - check what's on at LAX or Room4Dessert's late garden.

tagline: The skyline you already know, and five boroughs of everything else.

items.title: Brooklyn Bridge at sunrise
items.desc: Walk Brooklyn-to-Manhattan into the skyline - at 7am you share it with joggers, not tour groups.

items.title: Central Park loop
items.desc: Bethesda Terrace, the Mall and Bow Bridge - rent a bike or just drift for a morning.

items.title: The Met (pick three wings)
items.desc: Temple of Dendur, the armor hall, the rooftop in summer - it's pay-what-you-wish for NY state residents only, book otherwise.

items.title: The High Line + Little Island
items.desc: Elevated rail-line park from Hudson Yards to Chelsea Market, ending at the tulip-pier park.

items.title: Staten Island Ferry
items.desc: The free 25-minute ride past the Statue of Liberty - grab the right side going out, beer on board.

items.title: Bagel + slice fundamentals
items.desc: Everything bagel with scallion schmear in the morning, dollar-ish slice standing up at night.

items.title: Queens food crawl
items.desc: 7 train to Jackson Heights - momos, tacos, arepas and biryani within ten blocks.

items.title: West Village jazz
items.desc: Village Vanguard or Smalls - tiny rooms where the history is still being made, two sets nightly.

items.title: Bushwick warehouse night
items.desc: Brooklyn's club land - House of Yes for spectacle, Nowadays for the dance-floor purists.

tagline: Vertical ambition in the desert - gold souks on one side, sky lounges on the other.

items.title: Burj Khalifa at sunset
items.desc: Book the 124th-floor slot 30 minutes before sunset - day and night skyline in one ticket.

items.title: Old Dubai & the souks
items.desc: Abra boat across the creek for one dirham, then gold and spice souks in Deira.

items.title: Dubai Fountain show
items.desc: Every 30 minutes after dark at the Burj lake - watch from a lakeside terrace, free.

items.title: Desert safari + camp
items.desc: Dune bashing, camel ride and a Bedouin-style dinner camp under the stars - book afternoon-to-night.

items.title: Kite Beach morning
items.desc: Swim with the Burj Al Arab as backdrop, then the running track and food trucks.

items.title: Al Fahidi cafes
items.desc: Emirati breakfast - balaleet, chebab pancakes and karak chai in the wind-tower quarter.

items.title: Friday brunch
items.desc: Dubai's institution - bottomless everything for three hours; book somewhere on the Palm.

items.title: Sky-lounge circuit
items.desc: Cocktails at Atmosphere or Zeta Seventy Seven - smart dress, book windows seats ahead.

items.title: Marina dhow dinner cruise
items.desc: The mellow option - a wooden dhow drifting past the neon marina towers over dinner.

tagline: A medina maze of colour and noise that resolves, nightly, into the greatest square on earth.

items.title: Jemaa el-Fnaa at dusk
items.desc: Snake charmers give way to a hundred food stalls and drum circles - watch it ignite from a cafe roof.

items.title: Jardin Majorelle & YSL
items.desc: Cobalt-blue villa gardens and the Yves Saint Laurent museum - book the first morning slot.

items.title: Bahia Palace & Ben Youssef
items.desc: Zellige tilework and carved cedar at the palace, then the madrasa's perfect courtyard.

items.title: Souk deep-dive
items.desc: Get properly lost: leather, lanterns, carpets. Haggle from a third of the first price, smile always.

items.title: Hammam ritual
items.desc: Steam, black-soap scrub and mint tea after - Hammam de la Rose for gentle, a local bathhouse for real.

items.title: Atlas Mountains day trip
items.desc: Imlil village walks and waterfall trails under Mount Toubkal, an hour from the medina din.

items.title: Tanjia & tagine
items.desc: Marrakech's own dish - lamb slow-cooked in urns in the hammam ashes. Mechoui Alley does it daily.

items.title: Square food stalls
items.desc: Stall 31 and friends: grilled skewers, harira soup and snail broth if you're game.

items.title: Riad rooftop evening
items.desc: Gin and the call to prayer over a lantern-lit terrace - most riads let non-guests book dinner.

items.title: Comptoir Darna
items.desc: Dinner cabaret with belly dancers and a courtyard DJ - Marrakech's classic big night.

tagline: Mountains dropped into a city, beaches with a soundtrack, and samba until sunrise.

items.title: Christ the Redeemer early
items.desc: First cog train up Corcovado at 8am - clouds and crowds both roll in by ten.

items.title: Sugarloaf cable car
items.desc: Two cable cars to the granite dome - time it for sunset over Guanabara Bay.

items.title: Selaron Steps & Santa Teresa
items.desc: The mosaic staircase, then the tram-line lanes and studios of the hilltop artists' quarter.

items.title: Ipanema beach day
items.desc: Posto 9, a cadeira and endless vendors - caipirinha, queijo coalho, repeat. Sunset applause at Arpoador.

items.title: Pedra do Telegrafo hike
items.desc: The hanging-off-a-cliff photo (it's an illusion) plus wild beaches on the west side.

items.title: Feira de Sao Cristovao
items.desc: A northeastern-food fairground with forro bands - go Friday night, eat carne de sol.

items.title: Boteco crawl
items.desc: Rio's corner bars: ice-cold chopp, bolinhos de bacalhau and the game on - Jobi in Leblon is legend.

items.title: Samba in Lapa
items.desc: Rio Scenarium's antique-shop ballroom or the street party under the arches - Friday is peak.

items.title: Pedra do Sal samba circle
items.desc: Monday open-air samba at the birthplace of the genre - free, packed, magic.

tagline: Aztec ruins under colonial palaces under a street-food empire - the Americas' great megacity.

items.title: Zocalo & Templo Mayor
items.desc: The cathedral, the Aztec great temple dig and Diego Rivera's murals in the National Palace - one square.

items.title: Teotihuacan pyramids
items.desc: Climb the Pyramid of the Moon at opening - an hour north, go before the tour buses.

items.title: Frida Kahlo Museum
items.desc: The Casa Azul in Coyoacan - tickets sell out days ahead, book online then wander the plazas after.

items.title: Chapultepec & Anthropology Museum
items.desc: The Aztec sun stone and Maya rooms - arguably the best museum in the Americas, in the giant park.

items.title: Xochimilco trajineras
items.desc: Painted party boats through the canals with mariachis pulling alongside - go in a group, bring drinks.

items.title: Lucha libre night
items.desc: Masked wrestling at Arena Mexico - Tuesday or Friday, buy the cheap seats and a mask.

items.title: Taco omakase al pastor
items.desc: Trompo-carved al pastor at El Vilsito after 9pm, suadero at Los Cocuyos in Centro.

items.title: Mercado de Coyoacan
items.desc: Tostadas de tinga, esquites and pulque - a full market lunch for a few pesos.

items.title: Mezcaleria crawl in Roma
items.desc: Sip, don't shot - worm salt, orange slices, and Roma Norte's terraces until late.

items.title: Plaza Garibaldi mariachi
items.desc: Hire a song on the square, then tequila museum tastings - rowdy, touristy, essential once.

tagline: Two continents, five empires, one skyline of domes and minarets over the Bosphorus.

items.title: Hagia Sophia
items.desc: Fifteen centuries as cathedral, mosque, museum, mosque again - go at first prayer-break slot.

items.title: Blue Mosque & Basilica Cistern
items.desc: Iznik-tiled prayer hall, then the column forest of the sunken Byzantine cistern next door.

items.title: Topkapi Palace
items.desc: Ottoman treasury, the harem quarters and Bosphorus views from the fourth courtyard.

items.title: Bosphorus ferry to Asia
items.desc: Commuter ferry to Kadikoy - tea on deck, gulls chasing simit, a continent crossed for pocket change.

items.title: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar
items.desc: 4,000 shops under painted vaults - lokum tasting, lamp haggling, and getting lost is the point.

items.title: Hamam at Kilic Ali Pasa
items.desc: A 16th-century Sinan-built bathhouse - the full scrub-and-foam ritual under a marble dome.

items.title: Balik ekmek & meyhane night
items.desc: Fish sandwich off the boats at Eminonu by day; raki, meze and song at a Beyoglu meyhane by night.

items.title: Breakfast in Besiktas
items.desc: The Turkish kahvalti spread - forty small plates, endless tea, plan nothing before noon.

items.title: Karakoy & Galata bars
items.desc: Rooftops under the Galata Tower, then cocktail dens in the old bank quarter until 3am.

items.title: Nevizade Street
items.desc: One alley of stacked taverns off Istiklal - musicians work the tables, raki keeps arriving.

tagline: Harbour icons, ocean-pool mornings and coastal walks between the beaches.

items.title: Opera House & Harbour Bridge
items.desc: Circular Quay delivers both at once - take the Manly ferry for the classic water view back.

items.title: Bondi to Coogee walk
items.desc: Six clifftop kilometres linking beaches and ocean baths - swim at Bronte halfway.

items.title: Royal Botanic Garden
items.desc: Mrs Macquarie's Chair frames the Opera House against the bridge - free, best at sunrise.

items.title: Ocean pool swim
items.desc: Icebergs at Bondi is the famous one; Bronte Baths and Mahon Pool are the locals' church.

items.title: Blue Mountains day trip
items.desc: Two hours by train to Katoomba - Three Sisters lookout and eucalyptus valleys to the horizon.

items.title: Manly ferry + North Head
items.desc: The world's best commute, then a headland loop past old quarantine cliffs.

items.title: Fish market lunch
items.desc: Sydney Fish Market's deck - oysters, grilled barramundi and seagull defence tactics.

items.title: Chinatown & Spice Alley
items.desc: Lantern-lit hawker lane in Chippendale, then dumplings on Dixon Street.

items.title: Small bars of the CBD
items.desc: Hidden laneway bars - Baxter Inn's whisky wall, Cantina OK's mezcal shed. Start early, they're tiny.

items.title: Newtown on King Street
items.desc: Live bands, queer bars and late kebabs - Sydney's loosest strip since the lockout laws died.

tagline: The pyramids are just the opener - medieval Cairo and Nile evenings carry the show.

items.title: Giza pyramids & Sphinx
items.desc: Enter at opening, walk to the panoramic dune viewpoint, and pay extra to go inside Khufu once.

items.title: Grand Egyptian Museum
items.desc: Tutankhamun's full treasure hall by the pyramids - book timed tickets online.

items.title: Islamic Cairo walk
items.desc: Bab Zuweila to Al-Azhar down Al-Muizz street - a thousand years of minarets in one kilometre.

items.title: Khan el-Khalili bazaar
items.desc: Brass, spices and perfume oils in the medieval souk - mint tea at El Fishawy, open 24 hours since 1773.

items.title: Saqqara & Dahshur
items.desc: The step pyramid, the bent pyramid and empty desert sites the Giza crowds never reach.

items.title: Koshary at Abou Tarek
items.desc: Egypt's carb monument - pasta, rice, lentils, crispy onions and chilli vinegar in a four-storey shrine.

items.title: Nile-side fiteer
items.desc: Flaky Egyptian pancake-pie, sweet or savoury, best from a baladi bakery at midnight.

items.title: Felucca at sunset
items.desc: An hour under sail on the Nile with music and mint tea - haggle at the Garden City dock.

items.title: Zamalek terraces
items.desc: Nile-island neighbourhood of rooftop bars and jazz at Cairo Jazz Club - Thursday is the big night.
